column1: # One line per check. A line missing ANY field does not count as a result.
# control = did a positive control fire (something that must appear whether or not the feature works)
# alone   = was anything else driving on the same instance/directory at the time
# TIMESTAMP every row: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM, not just the date.
# ARM LABEL (added 2026-08-27 03:27 CEST). A two-arm A/B writes TWO rows and the parent arm is
#   SUPPOSED to FAIL — that failure is the proof the probe measures the defect, not a
#   result. Any query that takes "the latest row per cell" therefore reads a driven,
#   passing cell as failing; that happened to me twice on this file. So start the
#     [parent]  the pre-fix control arm. A FAIL here is EXPECTED and is evidence.
#     [fix]     the with-fix arm. THIS ROW IS THE VERDICT.
#     [single]  a one-armed reading with no pre-fix control (rarer; say why in the text).
#   Rows written before this note use prose forms such as "(PARENT arm)" / "(FIX arm)".
# 2026-08-26 16:05 CEST carry a date only; everything after carries the time.
# STALE = CODE changed since that commit, not merely that commits landed. Check with:
# Empty output means the row still counts. The first version of this rule said "behind the
# tip" and would have thrown away 25 valid rows over three docs-only commits.
